lesson_title: It Began With Words: Remembering the Holocaust
hook_text: Six million is too big a number to picture. So start with one girl, one diary, one hiding place behind a bookcase.
clip_script: Anne Frank was thirteen when her family hid behind a bookcase in Amsterdam. For two years they whispered by day while helpers brought food. She wrote about her dreams of becoming a writer. In 1944 they were betrayed. Anne died in a camp aged fifteen. She was one of about six million Jewish people murdered in the Holocaust. It did not start with camps. It started with words: lies about a people. Then laws took away their rights. Then walls: ghettos, families starving behind locked gates. Then killing squads, shooting whole communities beside pits. Then, in January 1942, a meeting by a lake in Berlin to organise what the Nazis called the Final Solution. Trains. Death camps. Auschwitz, Treblinka, Sobibór. Some people risked everything to save others. Most looked away. Remember the steps: words, laws, walls, murder. And remember that every step could have been stopped.
visual_style: A bookcase swings open to an attic room; a diary page in soft light; a simple sequence of icons appears in order: a speech bubble, a law book, a wall, a train track; candles light one by one.
pacing: Slow and steady throughout, with silences between the steps.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to understand how the Holocaust happened, who was responsible, and why we remember.
